column1: #desc;Aquila is a constellation on the celestial equator. Its name is Latin for 'eagle'
column2: and what it represents is mixed; some say it represents the bird that carried Zeus/Jupiter's thunderbolts in Greek-Roman mythology
column3: while others say it was the bird that Zeus ordered to attack Prometheus.
is one vertex of the Summer Triangle asterism.

column1: The constellation Aquila is best seen in the northern summer
column2: as it is located along the Milky Way. Because of this location
column3: many clusters and nebulae are found within its borders
column4: but they are dim and galaxies are few.
